inj_report.short: Lloyd rushed once for 10 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Wednesday's Week 12 loss to the Rams.
inj_report.long: After logging double-digit snaps in each of his first nine games of the season, Lloyd totaled just three offensive snaps Wednesday. In that context, his production was relatively efficient -- in fact, his 10-yard run on his lone carry put him just behind starting running back Kaleb Johnson, who tallied just 13 rushing yards on eight totes. With that said, it's hard to see a path to meaningful fantasy production for Lloyd if he doesn't get more opportunities, and he could be phased out of the game plan altogether if Josh Jacobs (finger) is able to return for the Packers' Week 13 matchup in New Orleans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

inj_report.short: Vidal carried the ball seven times for 36 yards and caught both his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
inj_report.long: After handling just four touches last week against the Ravens, Vidal saw his usage increase again as he recorded his most scrimmage yards since Week 5. This time, however, his additional volume came at the expense of Keaton Mitchell (knee), who left the game early. Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the Chargers' clear No. 1 RB over the last few contests, but if Mitchell's injury proves to be serious, Vidal could have some deeper-league appeal with the No. 2 role all to himself. He'll look to take advantage of whatever opportunities he gets in Week 12 against the Patriots.

inj_report.short: Coleman didn't catch his only target in Thursday's 13-10 win over the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: Coleman's involvement was minimal with DJ Moore healthy, as has been the case throughout the season. Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards Thursday, so none of Buffalo's receivers were particularly effective, but it would likely take another injury to Moore for Coleman -- who logged a 49 percent snap share in the contest -- to return to relevance in fantasy. Coleman hasn't exceeded 17 yards in a game or scored since Week 6. Up next for Coleman and the Bills is a Week 13 trip to New England.

inj_report.long: As his final numbers indicate, Johnson couldn't find any running room but was very productive with his one catch. The 2025 third-round pick of the Steelers was in the lead role once again with Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive, but Johnson couldn't come close to matching the encouraging rushing production he'd managed over the previous two games (24 carries, 110 yards, one TD). Jacobs is expected back for the Packers' Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6, a development that would relegate Johnson to his more customary reserve role.

inj_report.short: Mayer posted one catch (on four targets) for four yards during Sunday's 38-24 defeat at Denver.
inj_report.long: Mayer missed out on a prime opportunity with top TE Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) inactive in Week 11. When Bowers was out in Weeks 1 and 2 as he recovered from a meniscus trim in his left knee, Mayer went for a combined 9-55-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, but the latter also missed a stretch in the fourth quarter this Sunday due to a back injury. Bowers' status will be worth monitoring this week, as an absence from him next Sunday in Cleveland will set up Mayer for another key chance to produce.

inj_report.short: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
inj_report.long: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

inj_report.short: Fields caught two of his five targets for 25 yards in the Giants' 23-15 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Fields played 56 offensive snaps in the contest, logging 86 percent of the Giants' such plays. Despite the lack of catches, the No. 2 wide receiver continues to receive attention from quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a week-to-week basis.

inj_report.long: Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.

inj_report.short: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
inj_report.long: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

inj_report.short: Otton caught one pass for eight yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

inj_report.short: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
inj_report.long: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Fant (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, while Juwan Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out, Matthew Paras of the New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
inj_report.long: Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. The 29-year-old Fant has scored either three or four touchdowns in six of his eight NFL regular seasons, including three apiece in 2025 with Cincinnati and so far in 2026 with New Orleans. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp would be the next man up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

inj_report.short: Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
inj_report.long: Sadiq finished tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall behind wideout Garrett Wilson (five). The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for just the second time since catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score in Week 3 against the Lions. Sadiq has now caught 25 of 36 targets for 268 yards and a score while adding a three-yard rushing touchdown over the first 11 regular-season contests of his career.

inj_report.long: Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.

inj_report.long: Vele continues to run virtually every route for New Orleans, and the seven grabs matched his season high from Week 1 against the Lions, while Vele's 76 yards are a new high-water mark for the receiver. It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. The Saints offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. Vele is more of a low-ceiling fantasy WR4/5 most weeks.

inj_report.short: Bateman (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
inj_report.long: Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.

inj_report.short: Spann-Ford caught his lone target for 15 yards during Dallas' loss to the Eagles on Thursday.
inj_report.long: Spann-Ford served as the team's starting tight end for the third consecutive game as Jake Ferguson remains sidelined with a knee injury. However, Spann-Ford had a quiet outing but will look to play a larger role next week versus the Seahawks if Ferguson is out again.

inj_report.short: Shipley carried the ball 10 times for 46 yards and failed to catch his only target in Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys.
inj_report.long: Saquon Barkley (neck) exited the game early with a stinger, leaving the backfield in the hands of Shipley. The Eagles had to abandon the run game after halftime, however, limiting his usage as Joe Milton engineered an incredible comeback with his arm and legs. Barkley spent most of his time on the sideline trying to talk the coaching and training staffs into letting him back on the field, suggesting his absence was just precautionary, but if he misses additional action, Shipley could be in line for a much bigger workload in Week 13 against the Cardinals.

inj_report.long: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

inj_report.short: Daniels did not draw a target or log a touch Wednesday in a 26-13 win against the Packers.
inj_report.long: After posting a career-high 61 percent offensive snap share in Week 10 against Arizona, Daniels logged just a 22 percent share Wednesday. That was still good for third among Rams wideouts behind Konata Mumpfield (90 percent) and Xavier Smith (23 percent), but Daniels didn't get a pass thrown his way. If Davante Adams (hamstring) is able to return to action in Week 13 against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, Daniels' prospects for making an impact in the passing game will likely fall even further.

inj_report.short: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.
inj_report.long: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

inj_report.long: Pittman last played in Week 4 but is slated to be back in the lineup versus Denver after logging 'full' practice listings Tuesday through Thursday. In his return, Pittman will bolster a Pittsburgh WR corps that also features DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson, with the veteran pass catcher's Week 12 fantasy upside hinging on how well he connects with newly-installed starting QB Mason Rudolph. inj_report.short: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

inj_report.short: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season and therefore doesn't possess any fantasy relevance at the moment.

inj_report.short: Engram caught six of eight targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: It was easily Engram's best performance of the season, as he set season highs in targets, catches and yards against Las Vegas. Entering Sunday, Engram had produced just seven grabs for 48 yards total over his previous four games. Engram and the Broncos have a quick turnaround ahead of Friday's date with the Steelers. The tight end will be a low-floor fantasy option for that one.

inj_report.short: Bernard caught six passes for 40 yards on 10 targets in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing the team in playing time, especially if DK Metcalf gets disciplined for his latest on-field outburst.

It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.

inj_report.short: White turned two kickoff returns into 48 yards during Monday's 22-20 win over the Bengals.
inj_report.long: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.

inj_report.short: Washington caught all three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: The big tight end earned just a 6.8 percent target share on a day when Aaron Rodgers fired off 44 pass attempts in prolonged comeback mode. Washington has been held to 25 yards or fewer in eight of 10 games this season. He doesn't see enough volume to warrant weekly fantasy consideration as a touchdown-or-bust bet.

inj_report.long: Vaki once again filled a limited role as Jahmyr Gibbs continues to handle the bulk of the workload. The 25-year-old has totaled 181 rushing yards on 43 carries, in addition to catching 11 of his 13 targets for 84 yards across 11 games this season.

inj_report.short: Gadsden went without a target while taking the field for 23 of the Chargers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
inj_report.long: Gadsden ranked third in snaps among Chargers tight ends, finishing only slightly behind Charlie Kolar (30) and David Njoku (25). Despite arguably being the most talented pass catcher of the trio, Gadsden was the only one of the three who failed to draw a target in Week 11. The 2025 fifth-round pick has endured a disappointing sophomore campaign, having thus far put together a 20-179-1 receiving line on 30 targets over 10 games while topping 40 receiving yards on just one occasion.

inj_report.short: Jennings caught three of six targets for 20 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
inj_report.long: Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes, while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.

inj_report.long: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

inj_report.short: Iosivas (thumb) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
inj_report.long: Iosivas had his 21-day window to return from IR opened Nov. 12, so the Bengals are running out of time to add him back to the active roster before he would need to miss the remainder of the season. If Iosivas isn't added back onto the roster ahead of Sunday's game, expect such a move to transpire early the following week before the Bengals travel to Cleveland. Dohnte Meyers has been filling in as Cincinnati's No. 3 WR during Iosivas' ongoing absence.

inj_report.short: Brooks rushed once for four yards and caught four of five targets for 22 yards in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams.
inj_report.long: Brooks and Kaleb Johnson split the workload pretty evenly at running back for Green Bay, with the former logging 19 offensive snaps and the latter 24. Meanwhile, MarShawn Lloyd tallied just three snaps on offense. Whereas Johnson led the group with eight carries, Brooks was by far the most active in the passing game, tying for the overall team lead with both his five targets and four receptions. He had just four catches over five games coming into Wednesday, so it remains to be seen if the bump in work as a pass catcher continues for Brooks moving forward. The entire breakdown of the Packers backfield could shift in Week 13 against the Saints if Josh Jacobs (finger) is ready to return to action.

inj_report.short: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
inj_report.long: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

inj_report.short: Johnson rushed once for two yards and caught seven of his eight targets for 55 yards in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Johnson did not carry the rock much at all in the contest. The running back did, however, rank third in receiving yards for Buffalo behind Khalil Shakir (101) and DJ Moore (91). Johnson should continue to see receiving opportunities in Week 12 against the Chiefs as the Bills' preferred third-down back.

inj_report.short: TeSlaa failed to catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers.
inj_report.long: TeSlaa went without a reception for the second time in four weeks, and he has now gone six straight games without exceeding 20 receiving yards. The wide receiver played 23 snaps on offense, ranking third at his position behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (46) and Jameson Williams (45). TeSlaa will continue to be an unreliable fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup with the Bears on Thursday.

inj_report.short: Schoonmaker caught his lone target for six yards in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
inj_report.long: With Jake Ferguson (knee) remaining out for Dallas, Schoonmaker played 25 of 65 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford. Schoonmaker ran 12 routes, five fewer than Spann-Ford, and the duo combined to see three targets on a day Dak Prescott attempted 33 passes. Schoonmaker has five catches for 48 yards on six targets across nine games this season and has no fantasy appeal.

inj_report.short: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
inj_report.long: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Sample caught his lone target for nine yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
inj_report.long: After catching a touchdown pass from Joe Burrow in Week 10 against the Steelers, Sample saw only one target from the superstar quarterback during Monday's loss. Sample has caught one pass or zero in seven of 10 regular-season games and has an 11-72-2 receiving line on 12 targets while operating as the Bengals' TE2 behind Mike Gesicki.

inj_report.short: Njoku (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against New England.
inj_report.long: Njoku was held out of practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. He was cleared to return to practice in a limited capacity Friday, which was enough for the veteran tight end to to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden would both see expanded roles on offense in the event that Njoku doesn't play, and Patrick Herbert would be a candidate for elevation from the practice squad to give the Chargers more depth at tight end. That said, the Chargers' offensive potential figures to be limited in Week 12 in the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), with DJ Uiagalelei set to make his first career start.

The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

inj_report.short: Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
inj_report.long: Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

inj_report.short: Giddens will likely move up to the No. 2 RB role for the Colts in the short term, as Seth McGowan is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
inj_report.long: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that McGowan "will miss some time" but didn't specify how long the absence may be. For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.

inj_report.short: Williams carried twice for 18 yards and caught one of three targets for three yards against the Rams in a Thanksgiving Eve loss Wednesday.
inj_report.long: It was another rough performance for Green Bay's ground game, which gained just 55 yards on 14 carries. Williams got two totes, and the wide receiver ended up atop the team's rushing leaderboard with 18 yards, ahead of RBs Kaleb Johnson (13 yards on eight carries) and MarShawn Lloyd (10 yards on one carry). Williams has consistently seen minor work out of the backfield this season, logging at least one carry (but no more than three) in all but one of his six appearances. That gives a small boost to his fantasy outlook, but he's yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, so Williams is a very risky fantasy play. However, he'd probably get a boost in that regard if Christian Watson (concussion), who exited late in the first half Wednesday and didn't return, isn't able to suit up in Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

inj_report.short: Smith gained 11 yards on two carries and caught his only target for four yards in a 26-13 win against Green Bay on Wednesday. He added 15 yards on his lone punt return.
inj_report.long: Smith was used as a ball carrier for the first time this season and gained a chunk of yards on each of his totes. Aside from that, it was another quiet game for the third-year wideout, who hasn't really been able to take advantage of a wide open WR pecking order in the wake of injuries to star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring). In fact, Smith has logged less than a 25 percent offensive snap share over the past two games with the pair of stud WRs absent, so it appears head coach Sean McVay is looking elsewhere to fill the void. As such, Smith doesn't have much fantasy value given that his primary role is in the return game.

inj_report.short: Wilson caught three of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: It was Wilson's first game since suffering a finger injury in Week 5 that landed him on injured reserve. He ended up playing 49 of 71 offensive snaps, 39 of which came out wide. Wilson had primarily operated as the Steelers' slot receiver prior to his injury, but Germie Bernard has emerged in that role for Pittsburgh. While Michael Pittman (foot) is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, DK Metcalf might receive some form of team-imposed discipline after he had an on-field meltdown against the Eagles before being ejected from the game.

inj_report.short: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday.
inj_report.long: Shepard was elevated for Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers due to the absences of fellow wideouts Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). The veteran receiver answered the call by hauling in both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Since Shepard has now been elevated the maximum three times, he'll need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up again for the Jets this season.

inj_report.long: Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after drawing three targets in Week 10, as both Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace were clearly ahead of him Sunday.

inj_report.short: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

inj_report.short: Kolar brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Kolar was cleared to play Sunday after progressing through the league's concussion protocol, and his 30 offensive snaps were ahead of fellow tight ends David Njoku (25) and Oronde Gadsden (23). Kolar's eight-yard catch midway through the first quarter was the only pass that the fifth-year pro saw from Justin Herbert, but no Chargers pass catcher saw more than five targets other then Ladd McConkey (eight). Kolar has a 16-153-0 line on 24 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

inj_report.long: Mims reeled in just one pass for the second straight game, but his 36-yard snag in the second quarter was enough to notch his second-highest receiving yardage total in a contest this year. The wideout played just 15 snaps on offense, which ranked fifth at his position behind Courtland Sutton (49), Pat Bryant (40), Jaylen Waddle (39) and Troy Franklin (24) for Denver in Week 11. Mims will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of Friday's matchup with the Steelers.

inj_report.short: Metchie caught one of three targets for 19 yards during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Metchie and Bryce Young connected on a 19-yard pass late in the third quarter to set the Panthers up in the red zone, and the drive ended four plays later on a 33-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Metchie has caught one pass in each of his last two outings, and the fifth-year pro is firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the wide-receiver depth chart. The Panthers will hit the road in Week 12 for a crucial NFC South clash against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

inj_report.short: Williams (ribs) practiced fully Thursday, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
inj_report.long: Williams -- who was inactive in Week 11-- was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, but his full participation a day later paves the way for him to return to action Sunday against the Dolphins. With fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) in danger of missing his second straight game, Williams could end up working as the Jets' WR3 this weekend behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in the event that he's active and Cooper isn't.

inj_report.short: Donaldson logged a five-yard carry and brought in all four of his targets for 12 yards during the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
inj_report.long: Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. However, Donaldson coughed up the football on his first catch of the game early in the second quarter, which the Bears offense capitalized on with a six-play drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to D'Andre Swift. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

inj_report.long: Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth quarters, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).

inj_report.long: Loveland is seeking a second opinion on a knee injury he sustained in Chicago's 39-35 win over the Lions on Thanksgiving. Even if initial fears of a stint on IR prove overblown, Loveland is still considered week-to-week and could be in line for a multi-game absence, starting with Week 13 against the Jaguars. Since Cole Kmet (knee) is on IR, Roush and Stephen Carlson are Chicago's only healthy options at TE. Roush had five catches on as many targets for 31 yards after Loveland's early exit Thursday.

inj_report.short: Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
inj_report.long: The wide receiver filled a returner role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he could garner more opportunities on special teams following Sunday's success.

inj_report.short: Nailor caught one of five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.
inj_report.long: Nailor caught one pass for the second straight week, and he has exceeded 20 receiving yards only one time since Week 1. The wide receiver was unable to capitalize on the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle) in Week 11, and Nailor figures to remain an unattractive fantasy option in Week 12 against the Browns.

inj_report.short: Ahmed was elevated from the practice squad to the Bears' active roster Wednesday, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
inj_report.long: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was ruled out for Thursday's game, leaving the Bears with only two healthy options in the backfield going into Thanksgiving. With that, Ahmed will be up from the practice squad for the divisional tilt against the Lions.

inj_report.short: Restrepo caught his lone target for five yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
inj_report.long: Even with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) out, Restrepo played as the Titans' WR5 against Dallas, as his 17 offensive snaps trailed all four of Carnell Tate (61), Chimere Dike (53), Elic Ayomanor (36) and Calvin Ridley (26). Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.

inj_report.short: Cuevas caught one of three targets for eight yards during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.
inj_report.long: Cuevas continues to draw targets at an impressive clip, tallying three for his second straight game despite only being on the field for 14 of the Ravens' 61 offensive snaps in Week 11. Barring an injury to starter Mark Andrews or rookie fourth-rounder Matt Hibner, though, his role isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats. Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.

inj_report.short: Knox didn't catch his only target in Thursday's 13-10 win over the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: Knox finished without a catch while Dalton Kincaid caught both of his targets in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to thumb and ankle injuries. Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards in difficult weather conditions, but Knox hasn't contributed much as a pass catcher even when Allen has been slinging the ball effectively. Heading into a Week 13 trip to New England, Knox has caught 16 of 24 targets for 117 yards and one TD through 11 appearances.

inj_report.short: Trautman caught his only target for a one-yard touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 win versus the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Trautman leaked open behind Las Vegas' defense on a play-action pass from the goal line early in the second quarter, giving Denver a 10-0 lead. He still has a big role in the Broncos' offense, but he isn't running enough routes to sustain pass-catching production worth fantasy consideration in most formats.

inj_report.short: Wright carried the ball five times for 10 yards and returned three kickoffs for 79 yards during Miami's loss to the Bills on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Wright continues to struggle rushing the ball this season, averaging just 1.6 yards per carry across 30 rush attempts. The 23-year-old will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

inj_report.short: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

inj_report.short: Allen logged 80 kickoff-return yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Allen played 16 special-teams snaps in the contest. The running back did not log an offensive snap, leaving all the rushing work to Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright.

inj_report.short: Moreau brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
inj_report.long: Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those contests. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal unless Schultz were to miss time.

inj_report.short: Turpin failed to reel in his only target while rushing twice for 41 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans. He added 121 yards as a kick returner and logged a 13-yard punt return.
inj_report.long: Turpin went without a catch for the fourth time this season, but he was able to make his mark as a rusher in Week 11. The wideout was able to break loose for a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, notching his second score on the ground this season. Turpin has now caught five of 11 targets for 49 yards, rushed five times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added 695 kick-return yards and 121 yards as a punt returner over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

inj_report.short: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
inj_report.long: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Hibner recorded two catches for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
inj_report.long: Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.

inj_report.short: Meyers caught one of two passes for two yards, returned six kickoffs for 150 yards and returned one punt for five yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
inj_report.long: Most of Meyers' production came on special teams as a returner, and his one catch was his fewest since Week 7 against the Ravens, when he failed to record a reception. He's caught two passes or fewer in seven of 10 regular-season games, and his minimal role on offense would shrink even more once Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is cleared to return from injured reserve. The Bengals will head home for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

inj_report.short: The Steelers signed Hurleman off the practice squad to the active roster Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
inj_report.long: The move corresponds with the Steelers placing Ben Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve. Hurleman was called up from the practice squad and made his NFL regular-season debut against the Eagles in Week 11, when he caught six of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 19-16 loss for the Steelers. He also returned three punts for 36 yards and two kickoffs for 32 yards, and with Skowronek on IR, Hurleman figures to take on more return duties moving forward. His production in his NFL debut came after DK Metcalf was ejected from the game, and with Michael Pittman (foot) activated from IR, Hurleman figures to be limited to a return role for Friday's contest against the Broncos.

inj_report.short: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
inj_report.long: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.

inj_report.short: Coleman failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
inj_report.long: With Chris Bell (knee) back from his absence, Coleman reverted to WR4 duties for Miami, playing just 12 of 57 offensive snaps. He has no fantasy appeal while Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington and Bell are healthy. Coleman has been extremely inefficient through 10 games this season, catching just nine of 28 targets for 88 yards and two touchdowns.

inj_report.short: Hurst caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

inj_report.short: Franklin did not record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: The wide receiver did see two targets, but he wasn't able to haul them in. Franklin has just 17 targets across 10 games this year, recording nine catches for 100 yards and no scores.

inj_report.short: Delp hauled in his lone target for a six-yard reception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
inj_report.long: The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has handled a muted role at tight end behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant this season, compiling five receptions for 26 yards on five targets through nine appearances. Delp was limited to just 21 of the Saints' 72 offensive snaps in Week 11, but he could see his playing time pick up if the hamstring injury that knocked Johnson out of Sunday's loss early prevents him from suiting up this coming weekend in Cincinnati.

inj_report.short: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
inj_report.long: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.

inj_report.short: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.
inj_report.long: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.

inj_report.short: Allen caught two of four targets for 41 yards during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
inj_report.long: Allen was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after having done so only twice in the team's first eight games of the year. The wide receiver played 16 offensive snaps which ranked sixth at his position behind Xavier Worthy (47), Rashee Rice (32), Jalen Royals (24), Andrew Armstrong (20) and Josh Downs (17). As a result of the depth of the WR room in Kansas City, Allen will remain a hard fantasy option to trust Thursday versus the Bills.

inj_report.short: Whiteheart was listed as full participant in Cleveland's practice estimate Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
inj_report.long: Whiteheart popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a hip issue but should be good to go for Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has caught four of his seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown across 10 games this season.

inj_report.long: Bates went without a target for the fourth straight game. The 29-year-old's 21 offensive snaps ranked third at tight end behind Chig Okonkwo (49) and Ben Sinnott (24), and Bates should continue to have no fantasy value in Week 12 versus the Cardinals.

inj_report.short: Wright caught both of two targets for 42 yards during Sunday's 31-21 win versus the Buccaneers.
inj_report.long: One of Wright's two grabs in Week 11 was a 27-yard strike up the seam, easily his longest reception of the season thus far. He was on the field for 43 of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps Sunday, but he spent a substantial majority of those on blocking assignments for tailback Jahmyr Gibbs and company. His role in a Thanksgiving tilt versus the Bears may depend somewhat on the health of running mate Sam LaPorta, who was limited during Monday's walkthrough with an ankle issue.

inj_report.short: Bartholomew caught one of three targets for five yards in Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
inj_report.long: With T.J. Hockenson back in the lineup after being inactive Week 10, Bartholomew played just 18 of 67 offensive snaps as the Vikings' third tight end, also behind Ben Yurosek. Bartholomew has 11 catches for 95 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets across 10 games this season.

inj_report.short: Bellinger made one catch for five yards in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end capitalized on his sole target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.

inj_report.short: Watkins (groin) was estimated as a 'DNP' on Thursday's injury report, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
inj_report.long: The 49ers didn't hold a practice for Thanksgiving Day, but Watkins has been listed as a non-participant for the first two sessions of Week 12 prep due to a groin injury. He has one more opportunity to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. In the event that Watkins is not cleared to play against Seattle, more offensive snaps would be available for the likes of Jacob Cowing, Keenan Allen and Demarcus Robinson.

He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

inj_report.long: Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 wild-card win over the Jaguars last January.

inj_report.short: Jefferson failed to haul in his lone target during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.
inj_report.long: Jefferson could not hold onto a deep pass from Jayden Daniels early in the fourth quarter, and that catch would have set up the Commanders in the red zone. Jefferson has seen only one pass across his two outings since putting together a 5-58-1 receiving line on seven targets against the Rams in Week 9. Jefferson is firmly entrenched as the Commanders' WR4 behind Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks heading into Week 12 against the Cardinals on Sunday.

inj_report.short: Endries caught four of five targets for 33 yards during Monday night's 22-20 loss to the Commanders.
inj_report.long: Endries reeled in a career-high four passes while playing 15 snaps on offense in Week 11. The rookie is still behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample in the pecking order at tight end ahead of Week 12 versus the Saints.

inj_report.short: Farrell turned his lone target into a seven-yard reception in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.
inj_report.long: Farrell has suited up in each of the 49ers' first 10 games, but despite logging double-digit snaps in each contest, he's produced just four catches for 40 yards on seven targets. He'll continue to serve mainly as a blocking tight end on offense while also serving as a key contributor on the 49ers' special-teams units.

inj_report.short: Moore caught three of five passes for 57 yards during the Eagles' 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
inj_report.long: Moore got on the board with a 25-yard catch midway through the first quarter before connecting with Joe Milton on back-to-back passes for 23 and nine yards in the fourth, with Milton finishing that drive off on the next play with a 24-yard touchdown pass to rookie Makai Lemon. Moore's receptions, targets and yards were all season highs, and he could operate as the Eagles' WR3 behind Lemon and Darius Cooper for Week 13 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6, depending on the availability of DeVonta Smith, who injured his back late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game.

inj_report.short: Tucker didn't record any stats during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: Tucker didn't garner any touches on offense for the third straight week as Tampa Bay opted to use Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell exclusively in the backfield. Tucker will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as both Irving and Gainwell are available for the Buccaneers.

inj_report.short: Koziol went without a target while playing four of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
inj_report.long: The rookie fifth-round pick saw his streak of three straight games with a reception come to an end and also had his snap count decline for the fourth week in a row. Koziol ranked fourth in playing time among Jacksonville tight ends, marking the first time since Week 3 that he had played behind Quintin Morris (11 snaps Sunday).

inj_report.short: Adkins recorded a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Adkins was on the field for 30 of the Broncos' 73 snaps on offense, with his 41 percent share representing a season-high mark. The fourth-year tight end out of South Carolina has mainly served as a blocking specialist for Denver, having thus far been limited to a 7-47-3 receiving line on nine targets to go with a six-yard carry through 10 appearances on the season.

inj_report.short: Watkins caught one of his three targets for 26 yards during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
inj_report.long: Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.

inj_report.short: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.

inj_report.short: Sanders (hip) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
inj_report.long: Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.

inj_report.short: Sinnott played played 33 snaps (24 on offense, nine on special teams) but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.
inj_report.long: Chig Okonkwo was the Commanders' only tight end who produced offensively Monday, with the fifth-year pro catching four of five passes for 66 yards. Sinnott has been targeted zero times in seven of 10 regular-season games, with his lone productive outing being Week 10 against the Giants, when he brought in all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He brings very little fantasy appeal heading into Washington's Week 12 road tilt against Arizona on Sunday.

inj_report.short: Kacmarek went without a target while logging 21 of 57 snaps on offense in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
inj_report.long: After drawing at least one target in each of the previous three games, Kacmarek failed to draw a look from quarterback Kyle McCord, who connected with seven different pass catchers on the day. Kacmarek ran routes on just six of his 21 snaps, as the Dolphins continue to utilize him mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.

inj_report.short: Moore returned three kickoffs for 48 yards and one punt for 11 yards Wednesday in a loss to the Rams.
inj_report.long: Moore continued to serve as Green Bay's primary kick and punt returner, but he logged just one snap on offense. That limited usage as a receiver was even more concerning for his fantasy outlook given that star wideout Christian Watson couldn't play at all in the second half due to a concussion. Moore did notch 14 targets over his first five games, but since returning in Week 10 from a stint on IR, he's played just one offensive snap over two contests.

inj_report.short: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
inj_report.long: Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.long: Tolbert played just eight of the Dolphins' 55 offensive snaps in Week 11, and he drew just one target for the third time in his last five games. Miami will probably continue to lean primarily on Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell at wide receiver in a Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

inj_report.long: Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.

inj_report.short: McLaughlin was limited to one snap on offense and none on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
inj_report.long: Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.

inj_report.short: Ruckert went without a target while logging 16 of the Jets' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
inj_report.long: Since recording eight catches for 48 yards and a touchdown over the Jets' first three games, Ruckert has yet to draw a target in any of the team's subsequent eight contests. Ruckert's downturn in involvement in the passing game coincides with the Jets' top two tight ends -- Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq -- getting back to full health after they were either limited or sidelined in the early part of the season.

inj_report.short: Brown went without a target while playing eight of the Colts' 50 offensive snaps in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
inj_report.long: For the second week in a row, Brown ended up seeing more snaps on special teams (11) than offense. Through four games with Indianapolis, Brown has drawn just one target, which he turned into a seven-yard reception during a Week 6 loss to the Titans.

inj_report.short: The Broncos signed Schrader off the practice squad to the active roster Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
inj_report.long: Schrader reached the maximum three games of elevation from the practice squad, but now that he's on the active roster, the Missouri product is eligible to suit up for the Broncos moving forward. He's expected to contribute as a kickoff returner, and Schrader could also settle in as the No. 2 or 3 running back behind starter Jonah Coleman in Friday's game against the Steelers with J.K. Dobbins serving a one-game suspension.

inj_report.short: Mitchell recorded two receptions for 40 yards on two targets in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
inj_report.long: The fifth-year tight end was one of eight pass catchers that quarterback Dak Prescott connected with on the afternoon, with the pair of receptions marking Mitchell's first two grabs of the season. Mitchell took the field for 15 of the Cowboys' 65 snaps on offense, but he could wind up seeing most of his playing time on special teams once top tight end Jake Ferguson is cleared to return from the knee injury that has sidelined him for the past two games.

inj_report.short: Yurosek failed to draw a target while playing 29 of the Vikings' 67 offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers in Mexico City.
inj_report.long: Since being reinstated from injured reserve in Week 5, Yurosek has cleared 40 percent snap shares in five of the Vikings' ensuing six games. However, he remains a fringe part of the passing attack, having thus far mustered a 3-41-0 receiving line on four targets. He ran routes on just nine of his 29 snaps in Week 11, with Yurosek mainly serving as a blocker during his time on the field.

inj_report.short: Demercado rushed five times for 33 yards and caught both of his targets for minus-four yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.
inj_report.long: With Woody Marks (concussion) inactive, Demercado played the complementary role behind lead back David Montgomery, who rushed 26 times for 107 yards in his return from a multi-week groin injury. Demercado was picked up off waivers from Dallas last month.

inj_report.short: Thomas caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown during the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Thomas had the opportunity to step into the TE2 role behind Michael Mayer on Sunday due to the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps). Thomas' 35 offensive snaps were his most of the season, and he made his lone target from Fernando Mendoza count, with the duo connecting on a 19-yard touchdown pass late in the third quarter to tie the game up at 17-17. Thomas has seven catches on as many targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns through 11 regular-season games, although he would revert to being the No. 3 tight end in Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29 if Bowers is cleared to return for that contest.

inj_report.short: Latu recorded a 30-yard reception on four targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
inj_report.long: With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) inactive, Latu moved a rung up on the ladder at tight end and ended up seeing his most extensive playing time on offense of the season, logging 28 of 78 snaps (36 percent). He parlayed the elevated snaps into a season-high target count, but Latu's lone reception actually came on special teams, when Tommy Doman faked a punt and connected with the 24-year-old deep down the field for a fourth-down conversion. Latu will likely see his opportunities take a hit if Kincaid makes it back for a Thursday matchup with the Chiefs in Week 12.

inj_report.short: Etienne rushed six times for 29 yards, caught one pass for seven yards, logged 36 kickoff-return yards and recorded eight punt-return yards in the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the modest playing time, the running back made an impact across the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, whose role is as entrenched as any player at his position in the league.

inj_report.short: Morris went without a target while logging 11 of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
inj_report.long: For the first time since Week 3, Morris earned more playing time on offense than rookie Tanner Koziol (four snaps), who had previously been serving as the Jaguars' No. 3 tight end. Koziol offers more of a pass-catching threat at the position, but Morris is the superior blocker and also has a more integral role on special teams.

inj_report.short: Blue returned his lone kickoff for 23 yards but fumbled the ball in the process during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
inj_report.long: The loose ball was recovered by the Steelers, and Pittsburgh's offense turned that takeaway into a 40-yard field goal by Chris Boswell four plays later. It ended up being the only touch of the game for Blue, who played all 11 of his snaps on special teams. There's an outside chance he sees some involvement on offense against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day, but that will depend on the availability of both Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) and Will Shipley (foot/illness).

inj_report.short: James rushed twice for seven yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
inj_report.long: James went without a touch on offense for the majority of the game, but he was able to turn the team's final two carries of the game into seven yards late in the fourth quarter. The running back was on the field for five offensive plays, and he'll remain the team's No. 3 option behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black in Week 12 against the Seahawks.

inj_report.long: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.

inj_report.short: Melton finished Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams with one rush for three yards and two catches (on three targets) for 20 yards. He also returned two kickoffs for 31 yards.

However, he did step up a bit as a receiver, notching multiple receptions for the first time since he logged a season-high three catches in Week 5. Melton's main role this season has been as a kick returner, so he's well off the fantasy radar.

inj_report.short: Carlson caught two of his four targets for 30 yards during Chicago's win over the Lions on Thursday.
inj_report.long: Carlson hadn't caught a pass across his previous three appearances this season but benefited from increased playing time after Colston Loveland (knee) exited the game in the first quarter. Carlson could continue to see increased usage if Loveland is forced to miss extended time.

inj_report.short: Durham wasn't targeted while playing 15 of the Buccaneers' 69 snaps on offense and 15 on special teams in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: Durham's lone contribution in the box score came on the Buccaneers' first play of the day, when he recovered a fumble by quarterback Baker Mayfield. Though he's suited up for each of the Buccaneers' 10 games and has logged double-digit snaps on offense in the past six contests, Durham has recorded just one reception (for five yards) on two targets throughout the season. He's been deployed mainly as a blocking tight end, running routes on just 22 plays on the campaign.

inj_report.short: Lance failed to catch his only target and added 47 yards on kickoff returns during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
inj_report.long: Lance was unable to reel in a deep pass from quarterback Tyler Shough in the first quarter, and he didn't get another look the rest of the game. The wide receiver was on the field for 21 offensive snaps, ranking fourth at his position behind Devaughn Vele (64), Chris Olave (62) and Jordyn Tyson (36) in the contest. Lance will continue to primarily serve as a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward, making him an unattractive option for fantasy managers.

inj_report.long: Young reeled in his first pass since Week 3, and he notched his first career touchdown in the process. The wide receiver connected with quarterback Joe Burrow for a four-yard score in the third quarter, momentarily providing Cincinnati with a 17-10 lead. Young's 22 offensive snaps ranked third at his position behind Ja'Marr Chase (56) and Tee Higgins (56) while ahead of Dohnte Meyers (21), but Young may revert to a smaller role on offense with Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on track to return in Week 12.

inj_report.short: Sharp went without a target while logging 12 of the Buccaneers' 69 offensive snaps in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: Sharp's 17 percent offensive snap share placed him third among Tampa Bay tight ends, and he trails Cade Otton (97 percent) and Payne Durham (22 percent). The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU has rarely seen involvement in the passing game over his limited playing time on offense this season, recording a 21-yard reception on two targets over 10 appearances.

inj_report.short: Beck played all but one of his 13 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
inj_report.long: The 30-year-old Beck has been one of the more versatile players in the league this season. In addition to taking snaps as a fullback and tight end, Beck often serves as a short-kickoff specialist for the Jets, while also contributing on the special teams coverage and return units. While the variety of roles he handles makes him valuable from a real-life standpoint, Beck maintains little fantasy relevance. He's carried twice for one yard and has yet to draw a target through the Jets' first 11 games.

inj_report.short: Willis went without a target while logging nine snaps on offense and 21 on special teams in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.
inj_report.long: Willis has suited up in each of the 49ers' last nine games but has received little run on offense while the team's top two tight ends -- George Kittle and Luke Farrell -- have remained healthy throughout the season. The 27-year-old has logged single-digit snaps on offense in five straight contests and has yet to draw a target in 2026.

The veteran running back logged season highs with 15 carries and 81 yards against Arizona in Week 10, but all of that work came in garbage time. It appears Rivers isn't going to be a factor outside of his return duties while both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are healthy.

inj_report.long: Royals left the game in the third quarter and was ruled out not long afterward due to an ankle injury. The severity of the sprain will determine if Royals is in danger of missing any time. If that comes to pass for Royals, Andrew Armstrong likely will be on track for a few more offensive snaps behind Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen.

inj_report.long: Cowing saw limited action in the win, playing just six snaps on offense and two on special teams. The 25-year-old hasn't been targeted across the last two games and should continue to serve a depth role with Mike Evans now healthy.

inj_report.short: Washington (shoulder) will be out for Sunday's game against the Titans and is considered week-to-week moving forward, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
inj_report.long: Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

He started in each of the Seahawks' two games prior to the Week 11 bye, but is expected to revert to backup duties provided Sam Darnold (quadriceps) is cleared to start against the 49ers on Sunday. If Lock isn't available to play against San Francisco, then Jalen Milroe (illness) would be in line to operate as Seattle's QB2 behind Darnold.

inj_report.long: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

inj_report.long: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

inj_report.short: For now, Maye -- who suffered a fractured right fibula during a Week 10 loss to the Lions -- remains on the Patriots' 53-man roster rather than injured reserve, with coach Mike Vrabel citing the "balance" the team is hoping to strike with regard to managing its remaining designated to return from IR slots, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
inj_report.long: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

inj_report.short: McPherson made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
inj_report.long: After both teams went scoreless in a rainy first quarter, McPherson put the Bengals on the board with a 38-yard field goal in the second. He nailed a 56-yarder late in the fourth to give the Bengals a 20-19 lead, but his would-be game winner didn't come to pass as the Commanders raced down the field to set up Drew Stevens for a 26-yard field goal to seal the win for Washington. McPherson has made only five field goals (on six attempts) over the Bengals' last five games, but his 35 point-afters are second-most in the NFL behind Eddy Pineiro (36). The Bengals will head back home for Week 12 against the Saints, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in points allowed per game (25.7).

With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.

Reichard is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts through 10 regular-season games, and each of those misses have come from 50-plus yards. The Vikings will be home in a controlled environment for three of their next four games, starting in Week 12 against the Falcons on Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Boswell went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: This was a battle of Pennsylvania's kickers, as Boswell and Jake Elliott combined to account for 23 of the game's 35 points. Boswell was good from 25, 40 and 52 yards. The veteran kicker has been trending downward the last two seasons, and he entered play Sunday having made just 79.2 percent of his field-goal tries this season. After his perfect showing against the Eagles, Boswell has made all of his field goals in back-to-back games for the first time all season. On the year, he's 22-for-27 on FGAs and a perfect 18-for-18 on PATs.

inj_report.short: Smack made both of his field-goal tries and his lone extra-point attempt Wednesday in a loss to the Rams.
inj_report.long: Neither of Smack's field goals were chip shots; he nailed a 54-yarder late in the first quarter and a 48-yarder late in the second. The rookie entered Wednesday having gone just 15-for-21 on FG tries over his first 10 NFL games, so his accuracy Wednesday may have given him some needed job security. The most impressive aspect of Smack's rookie campaign has been his big leg. Despite his overall struggles, he's gone 4-for-5 on FG tries from 50-plus yards away.

inj_report.short: Smyth made two of three field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
inj_report.long: The Saints didn't have a scoring drive until the second quarter, when Smyth made his season-long, 56-yard field goal to cut the lead going into halftime, his first of two 50-plus-yard FGs in the game. The 25-year-old also continued his perfect PAT percentage for the season, making his singular attempt (5-for-5 in three games). His play on kickoffs stood out Sunday, committing two penalties for kicking the ball out of bounds and giving Chicago excellent field position.
